title: Maximum mean discrepancy with an RBF kernel
purpose: Compare two samples of vectors with the kernel maximum mean discrepancy: biased and unbiased estimators of MMD squared under a Gaussian kernel, the median-distance bandwidth, and a seeded permutation test. Use it to check whether two sets of outputs, embeddings or inputs come from one distribution.

entry_points.name: mmd_squared
entry_points.arguments: x_rows, y_rows: samples of equal dimension (up to 5000 rows each); bandwidth: sigma > 0 or null for the median heuristic; unbiased: bool

entry_points.name: median_bandwidth
entry_points.returns: the median of the positive pairwise distances

assumptions: Rows within each sample are exchangeable; under the null both samples come from one distribution.
The bandwidth is fixed before the permutations (the median heuristic uses the pooled sample, which permutations do not change).
guarantees: The biased estimate is non-negative and 0 for identical samples; the unbiased estimate is reported as computed, including negative values.
p = (1 + #{permuted statistic >= observed}) / (1 + B) is a valid p-value under exchangeability of the pooled sample.
Permutations use a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle driven by random() only.

known_wrong.name: unbiased_not_clamped
known_wrong.why: Clamping the unbiased estimate at zero (or taking its square root) biases it upward and breaks its expectation.

limits: Quadratic cost in the pooled sample size: a few thousand rows at most, and permutation tests multiply that by the number of permutations. One Gaussian kernel with one bandwidth; the median heuristic is a convention, not an optimal choice, and the test's power depends on it. Rejecting the null says the samples differ, not how or whether the difference matters.
technique_references: A kernel two-sample test (Gretton, Borgwardt, Rasch, Scholkopf and Smola)
Median heuristic for the Gaussian kernel bandwidth
Permutation tests with the (1 + count) / (1 + B) p-value
